    02 / TRANSACTION PREFLIGHT

    Don’t sign a black box.

    Paste a structured NEAR action preview. For a scanned account, KeySentry applies its restrictive policy before a wallet signature.

    • ADD FULL-ACCESS KEY → BLOCKED BY DEFAULT• DEPLOY CONTRACT → BLOCKED BY DEFAULT• DELETE KEY → REVIEW REQUIRED• UNKNOWN ACTION → FAIL CLOSED

    03 / TESTNET SIGNING LAB

    Prove the guard sits before the wallet.

    A genuine NEAR testnet wallet is optional for the safe-signature step. KeySentry first evaluates a decoded action. A full-access-key request is blocked without sending any request to the wallet; a self-transfer needs a second, explicit confirmation.

    • REAL TESTNET WALLET SELECTOR• NO SEED PHRASE OR PRIVATE KEY• 1 YOCTONEAR SELF-TRANSFER ONLY• IN-MEMORY KEYSENTRY SESSION

    CONTROLLED SIGNING DEMO

    NO WALLET CONNECTED · KEYSENTRY DOES NOT STORE A WALLET SESSION

    The public scanner never initializes a wallet. Connecting opens MyNearWallet, which may maintain its own session. A wallet is never called for a block; the self-transfer can use a tiny amount but still has testnet gas.

    WHAT IT PROTECTS AGAINST

    01

    Silent key changes

    Detect a new full-access key, a removed recovery key, or a function key that becomes broader than your baseline.

    02

    Permission attack paths

    Model the public receiver and method surface each key can reach, then identify where a changed contract needs revalidation.

    03

    Blind signing

    Translate visible transaction actions into irreversible consequences before the user approves them.
